sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Masterda Surya Sen**: Former school teacher who spearheaded the group, emphasizing strict discipline, moral integrity, and supreme sacrifice among young revolutionaries.
• **Indian Republican Army (IRA)**: Modeled intentionally on the Irish Republican Army to signify a formal, sovereign military challenge to British imperial authority.
• **Chittagong Armoury Raid**: Executed on **18 April 1930**, aimed at seizing two major armories to paralyze British communications, telegraph lines, and railway networks in East Bengal.
• **Jalalabad Hill Battle**: Fought on **22 April 1930**, where the revolutionaries entrenched themselves and engaged British troops in a pitched conventional military battle rather than fleeing immediately.
• **Mass Female Participation**: Unprecedented inclusion of women revolutionaries such as **Pritilata Waddedar** (who led the European Club attack at Phartali) and **Kalpana Datta** (arrested and tried alongside Surya Sen).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Chittagong District (East Bengal / modern Bangladesh)**: Epicenter of the revolt, featuring isolated hills, coastal access, and dense railway junctions.
• **Dhalghat & Patiya Hideouts**: Rural interiors used for protracted guerrilla warfare after the initial urban armoury raids.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Lack of widespread mass peasant mobilization on an ideological agrarian platform; severe British counter-insurgency repression and intelligence penetration.
• **Policy Interventions**: Post-independence state recognition, historical rehabilitation of revolutionary memorials, and incorporation into mainstream nationalist historiography.

items.title: Mnemonic for Chittagong Chronology
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'S P J K' -> **S**urya Sen plans, **P**hartali attacked, **J**alalabad fought, **K**alpana captured.
• **Decoded Meaning**: Captures the life cycle of the Chittagong uprising from 1930 planning to subsequent female-led operations and trials.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly organizes events from 1930 to 1933 in correct chronological sequence.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: 1930 = Armoury Raid + Jalalabad Battle; 1932 = Pahartali Club Raid (Pritilata); 1934 = Execution of Surya Sen.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently attributes the Chittagong Armoury Raid directly to the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). Remember, HSRA operated primarily in Northern India (Punjab, UP, Delhi), whereas the Chittagong Revolt Group was an independent regional organization in Bengal led by Surya Sen.

Mains Value Addition: In answers dealing with gender equality and women's emancipation in the freedom struggle, explicitly cite Pritilata Waddedar and Kalpana Datta to demonstrate how revolutionary movements broke orthodox patriarchal barriers by involving women in armed combat roles.

keyTakeaways: The Chittagong Revolt Group (IRA) under Surya Sen marked the pinnacle of organized revolutionary military action in Eastern India during 1930.
The movement uniquely integrated revolutionary youth and women (Pritilata Waddedar, Kalpana Datta), expanding the social base of militant nationalism.
Despite military defeat at Jalalabad Hill, the group demonstrated unmatched tactical defiance and inspired generations of nationalists.
